items.item: [iOS-02] Dev machine — Xcode + Flutter SDK + CocoaPods
items.description:
## Intended Outcome
Mac ready for Flutter iOS builds.

## Step-by-Step
1. Install Xcode from Mac App Store (you'll never open it)
2. Accept license: `sudo xcodebuild -license accept`
3. Clone Flutter: `git clone https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git -b stable`
4. Add to PATH, `flutter precache --ios`
5. `sudo gem install cocoapods`
6. `flutter doctor`

## Why Xcode?
You never open it. Flutter calls Xcode's toolchain behind the scenes:
- `flutter run` calls Xcode build system automatically
- `flutter build ipa` signs and archives via Xcode tools
- Only time you open Xcode: Organizer > Distribute App (30 secs)
Your workflow stays 100% in Flutter/VS Code.

## Skills/Tools Required
- `flutter-building-layouts` -> `.agents/skills-archive/flutter-building-layouts/SKILL.md`

## Audit (EOD Report-Back)
Append findings to .pi/EOD_AUDIT.md: (1) files changed, (2) verification results, (3) gaps/findings, (4) decisions, (5) estimated tokens.

items.item: [BUG] Simulator glucose engine calibration produces unrealistically high baselines
items.subject: [BUG] Simulator glucose engine calibration produces unrealistically high baselines
items.description:
Sim anchor profiles (especially "well_controlled") generate glucose values pegged at 400 mg/dL ceiling, preventing pattern detectors from finding meaningful spikes. Detector requires ≥50 mg/dL rise, but capped values show only ~4 mg/dL rise. Investigate glucose engine calibration, anchor config, and capping logic.

SQL evidence from user 657 (run 29):
- 2016 blood_glucose readings, nearly all at 400 mg/dL
- Pre-meal average ~396, peak ~400 (capped)
- Detector spike_threshold = 50 → glucose_rise = 4 → never fires
- All 16 completed runs show 0% detection rate

Acceptance Criteria:
- "well_controlled" anchor generates realistic glucose (e.g., 80-160 mg/dL)
- Pattern detectors can find actual spikes in sim data (non-zero detection rate)
- Glucose engine calibration produces distinct post-meal rises of ≥50 mg/dL
- No regression in other anchor types

items.item: [FOOD] Improve food search quality — OFF ranking, manual entry, curated staples
items.subject: [FOOD] Improve food search quality — OFF ranking, manual entry, curated staples
items.description:
Open Food Facts search returns poor matches for common foods (e.g., "butter" → peanut butters, "fried eggs" → gummy candy). Need multiple entry paths: manual food entry, ingredient-level parsing, curated staples table, brand/region filtering, and confidence-based fallbacks.

Current issues:
- "fried eggs" → gummy candy products (OFF is barcode/Collaborative DB, not recipe matcher)
- "butter" → peanut butter, almond butter (dairy butter deprioritised)
- "Warburtons" → brand matches but "thick sliced" doesn't always resolve
- No manual entry fallback when search fails

Acceptance Criteria:
- "3 fried eggs + Warburtons toast + butter" resolves to ~60g protein, ~30g fat, ~50g carbs
- Butter search biases to dairy butter, deprioritises nut spreads
- Manual/custom food entry path exists with template defaults
- Common meals saveable as one-tap presets
- Curated "core staples" table for breakfast/lunch/dinner basics
- Country+category filtering applied to OFF queries
items.activeForm: improving food search quality — OFF ranking, manual entry, curated staples

items.subject: [CAL] Fix cumulative drift across all anchors
items.description: Meals don't fully recover to baseline before the next meal, causing baseline to creep from 118→154→163 across the day. This fix is needed before batch-calibrating remaining anchors because the drift affects all of them.
